basis: Seven findings reassessed on 8 October: four ownership/reference findings after the recorded-contents corrections, then F17/F20/F21 after descriptor-based compression identification and shared audio-summary field decoding. Each stage links its own primary/genuine evidence, authored controls, native verification and 2,413-row read-only comparison. The other 33 assessments retain their original evidence and limits.

findings.title: 2.14 fixed point is displayed as Float
findings.mechanismAndEvidence: Canon combines the complete coding label with component depth; depth 254 produces 16-bit S2.14 for the fixed label and 32-bit Float for the standard label. Bit Depth and Sample Format are independent observations. [MXF `numericFormat` / descriptor projection](../src/canon/mxfprojection.cpp), [OMF technical projection](../src/canon/omfprojection.cpp); `fixed_and_float_sentinels_and_alpha_are_independent` in [MXF projection tests](../tests/tst_canon_mxfprojection.cpp), `dnxUncompressedFlavour` in [OMF projection tests](../tests/tst_canon_omfprojection.cpp); [genuine-media comparison, Bit Depth corrections](full-scan-comparison-2026-10-07.md), [RDD/specimen evidence](dnx-codec-evidence.md).
findings.limits: The interpretation is qualified by coding label/depth; it does not certify every descriptor/essence combination. Historical old-helper assertions are not live behavior.

findings.title: RGBA component depths are mostly ignored
findings.mechanismAndEvidence: MXF projects the complete eight-slot PixelLayout, treats padding/terminators separately and labels differing depths. OMF keeps component-code/size arrays and derives a uniform depth only when their non-fill widths agree. Alpha is independent. [MXF `projectPixelLayout`](../src/canon/mxfprojection.cpp), [OMF RGBA projection](../src/canon/omfprojection.cpp); `fixed_and_float_sentinels_and_alpha_are_independent` in [MXF tests](../tests/tst_canon_mxfprojection.cpp), `rgbaAlphaEvidence` / `uncompressedAlphaRequiresExplicitEvidence` in [OMF tests](../tests/tst_canon_omfprojection.cpp); [eight genuine formerly blank 16-bit rows](full-scan-comparison-2026-10-07.md).
findings.limits: Palette/unknown layouts need separate interpretation; OMF mixed component widths remain in raw arrays rather than a fabricated scalar depth. Alpha presence does not prove transparent pixels.

findings.title: Stored, sampled and display geometry are collapsed
findings.mechanismAndEvidence: Original rectangles and offsets survive in the graph. The user-approved Resolution policy selects validated visible geometry, applies format-specific coordinates/layout, and retains the narrow specimen-backed proxy exception. [shared geometry selector](../src/canon/picturegeometry_p.h), [MXF projection](../src/canon/mxfprojection.cpp), [OMF projection](../src/canon/omfprojection.cpp); `visible_resolution`, `nested_crop_offsets` in [MXF tests](../tests/tst_canon_mxfprojection.cpp), `visibleResolution` / `verifiedProxyResolution` in [OMF tests](../tests/tst_canon_omfprojection.cpp); [policy and complete 2,413-row verification](visible-resolution-2026-10-07.md).
findings.limits: No square-pixel conversion or universal player-presentation claim. Other geometry stays in RAM; a separate detail UI is outside the agreed v1 scope.

findings.title: Padding and field-height rules are promoted to universal facts
findings.mechanismAndEvidence: No unconditional 1088→1080 or 544→540 normalization remains in the live geometry selector. Explicit valid crops choose visible dimensions; absent/unreadable/conflicting fields are distinguished. MXF layouts and the separately retained OMF1 convention have different rules. [geometry selector](../src/canon/picturegeometry_p.h), [format-specific projections](../src/canon/mxfprojection.cpp), [OMF projection](../src/canon/omfprojection.cpp); no-crop padding, single/mixed/segmented layouts, offsets and overflow rows in [MXF tests](../tests/tst_canon_mxfprojection.cpp) / [OMF tests](../tests/tst_canon_omfprojection.cpp); [current geometry policy/evidence](visible-resolution-2026-10-07.md).
findings.limits: OMF legacy partial rectangles use explicitly explained toolkit compatibility defaults; the narrow proxy exception is an inference for seven verified configurations. Neither is generalized to arbitrary writers.

findings.title: MXF graph traversal follows ordinary 16-byte values
findings.mechanismAndEvidence: The reader creates relationships from registered strong/weak-reference types after Primer identification. Generic weak references remain unresolved. The only special DataDefinition edge requires a unique dictionary DataDefinition target and is marked Derived. Projectors follow named relationship properties rather than arbitrary byte lengths. [schema-driven `addReferences`](../src/canon/mxfobjects_p.cpp), [named traversal](../src/canon/mxfprojection.cpp); `weakReferenceDoesNotGuessInstanceUidTarget`, `repeatedPartitionsKeepReferenceScope`, `relocatedPrimerAndNoTagGuess` in [fresh-reader tests](../tests/tst_canonmxf.cpp); [independent schema/reader evidence](fresh-mxf-reader-2026-10-04.md).
findings.limits: This closes ordinary-UL false ownership edges. It does not prove all target-class/track applicability or graph completeness; decisive incomplete-list behavior remains F06.

findings.title: Missing MXF references silently disappear
findings.mechanismAndEvidence: MXF decisive reference paths validate each retained occurrence, resolved target class/identity and partition before projecting dependent descriptor/master/component/origin facts. Broken Tracks no longer supplies master name, association or duration. Raw unresolved relationships remain. See [correction report](root-membership-corrections-2026-10-08.md), [MXF controls](../tests/tst_canon_mxfprojection.cpp), [independent rooted counterexamples](evidence/root-membership-mxfprojection-2026-10-08.json) and [final 38-suite receipt](evidence/root-membership-full-tests-2026-10-08.txt).
findings.limits: This closes readable-subset selection, not exact source-track/start/slot/timecode evaluation (F15/F16) or every custom component schema. No genuine malformed-reference specimen is certified.

findings.title: Repeated MXF PackageUIDs overwrite the lookup
findings.mechanismAndEvidence: Active package lookup keeps all known identity claims and treats unknown/unreadable claims as unresolved candidates. Contradictory active claims cannot disappear and restore uniqueness. Ownerless carriers preserve positive identity conflicts through projection and PMR/MDB reconciliation. The fresh authored counterexample selects no owner and records a Conflicting blank identity. See [correction report](root-membership-corrections-2026-10-08.md), [counterexample](evidence/root-membership-mxfprojection-2026-10-08.json), [MXF tests](../tests/tst_canon_mxfprojection.cpp) and [scan integration controls](../tests/tst_canonscan.cpp).
findings.limits: The tested conflict cases are authored; no genuine contradictory PackageUID specimen is claimed. An unreadable identity remains unknown rather than becoming a fabricated positive disagreement.

findings.title: Primer-less tag recovery has the same output confidence
findings.mechanismAndEvidence: Unmapped/ambiguous local tags keep bytes and no decoded meaning; missing Primer mappings qualify the source as Incomplete. Private properties require their established mapped identity. There is no canonical-fixed-tag semantic fallback in the live reader. [Primer/local-item reader](../src/canon/mxfreader.cpp), [mapped type interpretation](../src/canon/mxfobjects_p.cpp); `relocatedPrimerAndNoTagGuess`, `ambiguousPrimerRetainsBytes`, `missingPrimerMappingQualifiesSource` in [reader tests](../tests/tst_canonmxf.cpp); [reader contract](fresh-mxf-reader-2026-10-04.md).
findings.limits: Narrower supported parsing is deliberate: unprimed bytes remain evidence but cannot establish the old recovered facts. Unknown/private types remain uninterpreted.

findings.title: Several MXF property types accept the wrong lengths
findings.mechanismAndEvidence: Schema `fixedSize` requires exact scalar/compound widths; malformed typed values remain Unreadable and qualify source completeness. Picture geometry uses wide integers. Selected UInt32 ChannelCount still reaches the UI adapter's unchecked `toInt()` narrowing. [exact type decoder](../src/canon/mxfobjects_p.cpp), [property catalogue](../src/canon/mxfcatalogue_p.h), [channel projection](../src/canon/mxfprojection.cpp), [adapter Channels conversion](../src/canonadapter.cpp); authored width probe below rejects 20-byte UL and 5-byte UInt32 against valid-width controls.
findings.limits: The unsigned-to-int range aspect remains: a valid UInt32 channel value outside `int` range is not explicitly rejected/qualified before projection to `MediaFile::channels`. Probe coverage is bounded, not every type width.

findings.title: 4–8 byte duration “flavours” are not established MXF types
findings.mechanismAndEvidence: Registered MXF Length is a signed Int64 with exactly eight value bytes. The fresh live reader has no 4–7-byte duration-flavour compatibility assertion. Raw invalid bytes survive with a type-width explanation. [Length→Int64 catalogue entry](../src/canon/mxfcatalogue_p.h), [exact decoder](../src/canon/mxfobjects_p.cpp); fresh-source authored width probe below: five-byte Length Unreadable/Incomplete, eight-byte control Present/Complete.
findings.limits: No new support for short-width manufacturer serialization is claimed.

findings.title: Numeric resolution IDs fabricate codec ULs
findings.mechanismAndEvidence: Canon's `knownDnxLabel` admits a finite explicit set, not the whole 1235–1489 interval; unknown IDs remain raw without a synthetic label. A recorded usable coding property takes precedence; malformed/present coding does not masquerade as absence. [`knownDnxLabel` / coding projection](../src/canon/omfprojection.cpp), [DNx profile catalogue](../src/canon/dnxnames_p.h); exact operating-point and verified decimal-clock controls in [OMF projection tests](../tests/tst_canon_omfprojection.cpp); [mapping/evidence limits](dnx-codec-evidence.md).
findings.limits: This closes arithmetic label fabrication, not catalogue completeness. For example 1256 is not in Canon's numeric fallback subset; a missing recorded label cannot be filled merely because the historical audit cited another mapping.

findings.title: Legacy text decoding can silently change the text
findings.mechanismAndEvidence: Raw text/encoding evidence is unchanged. Declared UTF-8 is validated; unlabelled text can use the user-approved explicit UTF-8 inference and legacy OMF/MDB MacRoman fallback, each retaining Derived basis, encoding and explanation. PMR legacy non-ASCII does not inherit universal MacRoman. [`withInferredText` / observations](../src/canon/projection.cpp), [OMF projection](../src/canon/omfprojection.cpp), [reader text interpretation](../src/canon/omfobjects_p.cpp); `textEncodingIsPerProperty` in [MDB tests](../tests/tst_canonmdb.cpp), `inferredUtf8RetainsOriginalEvidence` / `inferredMacRomanFallback` in [OMF tests](../tests/tst_canon_omfprojection.cpp); [confirmed current policy](text-encoding-names.md).
findings.limits: An inferred readable spelling does not prove the writer's undeclared codepage. Windows and other legacy encodings remain unestablished.

findings.title: Repeated OMF/MDB mob records choose the first descriptor and values
findings.mechanismAndEvidence: Mobs index to all object handles; every linked supported descriptor creates a candidate. Repeated/editorial observations survive; multiple master associations are preserved. Equal-priority incompatible selected facts remain unresolved, while compatible duplicate duration facts can coalesce without discarding evidence. [OMF/MDB candidates and attributes](../src/canon/omfprojection.cpp), [scan selection](../src/canon/scanengine.cpp); `repeatedDescriptorsAndMastersRemainSeparate`, `repeatedFactsRemainConflicting` in [projection tests](../tests/tst_canon_omfprojection.cpp), `incomplete_or_conflicting_table_metadata_reads_header`, `clip_duration_coalesces_duplicate_facts_without_discarding_evidence` in [scan tests](../tests/tst_canonscan.cpp); [approved priorities](live-connection-2026-10-04.md).
findings.limits: Candidate retention does not establish HEAD membership (F14), full source-track applicability (F15/F16), or the truth of fresh/stale alternatives. No genuine contradictory duplicate specimen is claimed.

findings.title: OMF HEAD indexes and media-object classes are bypassed
findings.mechanismAndEvidence: OMF projection establishes typed OmfRevision, required OMF1 ObjectSpine or OMF2 HEAD:Mobs/MediaData membership, optional legacy-index qualification and class-specific root-listed MediaData identities. Physical headers need a positive recorded media-data identity; database/native audio observations stay independent. Unlisted duplicate records in a genuine legacy MDB and the three EDIT databases are excluded from owned metadata while retained raw. See [specimens](root-membership-specimens-2026-10-08.md), [corrections and corpus comparison](root-membership-corrections-2026-10-08.md), [OMF tests](../tests/tst_canon_omfprojection.cpp) and [scanner fixtures](../tests/tst_scanner.cpp).
findings.limits: Unknown OMF revisions/classes and damaged required membership stay unqualified. A 12-byte MobIndex/32-byte Avid UID conversion is not proven; both survive and object references establish membership. UID-width codec inference and audio-summary extension defects remain F17/F20/F21.

findings.title: OMF timecode is the first TCCP found anywhere in ancestry
findings.mechanismAndEvidence: Canon collects all explicit drop flags through recorded component/source-ID relationships and retains conflicts; an unrelated unlinked TCCP cannot select a value. The former first-TCCP start-timecode assignment is absent from the live model. [`components`, `sourceMobs`, `timecode`, `trackDurations`](../src/canon/omfprojection.cpp); `associatedTimecodeAndClipDuration` in [projection tests](../tests/tst_canon_omfprojection.cpp); [current timecode boundary](live-connection-2026-10-04.md).
findings.limits: SourceTrackID, source start, slot origin and branch applicability are still not evaluated by `timecode`; all source tracks/alternates can contribute. Applicable start timecode is unavailable rather than implemented. Full semantic timeline evaluation is outside agreed v1 scope, but current drop provenance remains narrower than that proof.

findings.title: A single OMF mob rate is an insufficient multi-slot model
findings.mechanismAndEvidence: Every slot's recorded rate survives; linked master track durations now carry TrackId, their own length and clock. File-level `editRate` still requires all MSLT slot clocks to agree and is used for audio display timing. [`editRate` / `trackDurations` / descriptor duration](../src/canon/omfprojection.cpp); `associatedTimecodeAndClipDuration`, `legacySequenceClipDuration`, `genuineDatabaseSequenceDurations` in [projection tests](../tests/tst_canon_omfprojection.cpp); [Clip Duration paired evidence](evidence/clip-duration-database-evidence-2026-10-07.json).
findings.limits: Relevant essence-slot selection is not implemented for differing file-mob clocks. No genuine standard OMF2 multi-rate specimen or decisive regression establishes that boundary.

findings.title: Identifier width is used as a media-era discriminator
findings.mechanismAndEvidence: MobId storage width no longer participates in compression lookup. The admitted legacy mapping requires descriptor class, exact Compression/DIDResolutionID property types and verified pairs; a present coding label permits refinement only for exact corroborated compatible labels. Unknown or differing coding stays independently retained without private override. [implementation and primary evidence](legacy-compression-and-audio-summaries-2026-10-08.md), [typed mapping](../src/canon/omfprojection.cpp), [genuine pairs/resources](evidence/legacy-compression-pairs-2026-10-08.json), [two real DV name refinements](evidence/legacy-audio-dv-name-evidence-2026-10-08.json), [projection tests](../tests/tst_canon_omfprojection.cpp). Final native suites: 39/39; real scan: 2,413 identical paths and only two supported DV short-name changes.
findings.limits: The exact 32-byte-owner/JFIF independence control is authored; genuine inspected JFIF owners are 12-byte. The real 32-byte-owner DV refinements independently demonstrate width-free lookup for their verified pairs. Only the finite corroborated mapping subset is admitted; unverified DV100 IDs are excluded. Naming refinement does not prove earlier genuine DV rows identified a different encoding family.

findings.title: Private AUID conversion assumes little-endian numeric fields
findings.mechanismAndEvidence: Canon now converts AUID numeric fields according to the property's metadata byte-order context. This removes the unconditional little-endian branch, but does not by itself establish the private property's declared serialization. [`auidToUl` / `uniqueRaw EssenceCompression`](../src/canon/omfprojection.cpp); authored big-endian `dnxUncompressedFlavour` in [projection tests](../tests/tst_canon_omfprojection.cpp); [metadata byte-order evidence/limits](fresh-mdb-reader-2026-10-04.md).
findings.limits: No genuine big-endian private EssenceCompression specimen or traced authoritative private-property serialization is established in the current proof reports. The authored fixture encodes the implementation's expectation; it cannot settle this verification gap.

findings.title: Standard OMF locator classes are omitted
findings.mechanismAndEvidence: The new reader preserves named DOSL/NETL/TXTL property bytes/types if present, instead of dropping the objects. The source-path projector still admits only MACL/WINL/UNXL `_SRCFILE` targets and a narrow path-property list. [all-property reader](../src/canon/omfobjects_p.cpp), [source-locator projection](../src/canon/omfprojection.cpp); retained unknown/private-property cases in [MDB tests](../tests/tst_canonmdb.cpp), [schema omission evidence](../docs/reviews/2026-10-03-format-audit/format-audit.txt).
findings.limits: No typed locator-kind interpretation or SourceFilename projection for DOSL/NETL/TXTL, no targeted specimen regression, and no documented user acceptance of that exact locator subset. URL/text hints must not become fabricated filesystem paths.

findings.title: WAVE valid bits and subtype are ignored
findings.mechanismAndEvidence: Native WAVE fmt and OMF/MDB WAVD Summary fmt chunks now share one field decoder. Storage width, valid precision, Samples union, channel mask and SubFormat survive as separate original-byte/range/read-state observations. Known PCM/IEEE float subtypes qualify valid-bit interpretation; unknown, missing or invalid precision cannot be selected merely from storage width. [implementation, Microsoft semantics and verification](legacy-compression-and-audio-summaries-2026-10-08.md), [shared decoder](../src/canon/audioreader_p.cpp), [projection](../src/canon/omfprojection.cpp), [genuine decoded Summary receipt](evidence/audio-summary-decoded-evidence-2026-10-08.json), [reader tests](../tests/tst_canonlegacy.cpp), [projection tests](../tests/tst_canon_omfprojection.cpp).
findings.limits: No genuine extensible-WAVE Summary was found in the inspected corpus. Its valid-bit, GUID, channel-mask and malformed-extension controls are authored against the published WAVE structure. Genuine PCM summaries and their original hashes are checked; this does not certify every WAVE subtype or historical Avid writer.

findings.title: AIFF/RIFF summary validity is weaker than chunk validity
findings.mechanismAndEvidence: Summary interpretation requires the exact supported property/type and matching RIFF/WAVE or FORM/AIFF/AIFC family, checks copied metadata bounds, and shares native field decoding. It deliberately stops at omitted sample data rather than demanding a full recording. Individual extension/name failures retain their bytes and Unreadable state without discarding independently readable base fields. Original Bento framing outcome remains distinct from audio-field interpretation. [implementation/specification/evidence report](legacy-compression-and-audio-summaries-2026-10-08.md), [decoder](../src/canon/audioreader_p.cpp), [MDB attachment](../src/canon/omfobjects_p.cpp), [genuine Summary provenance](evidence/audio-summary-decoded-evidence-2026-10-08.json), [projection tests](../tests/tst_canon_omfprojection.cpp). All three genuine Summary byte hashes remain identical; AIFF-C compressionName is separately decoded at offset10523/length14.
findings.limits: Missing GUID/name, malformed bounds and contradictory Summary controls are authored, not claimed damaged real Avid specimens. The supported Summary copy is not treated as a complete native file. Readable fields can remain usable while independent fields are unreadable; no corruption recovery or universal Summary writer certification is claimed.

findings.title: PMR timestamps establish a cache heuristic, not current content
findings.mechanismAndEvidence: [PMR reader](../src/canon/pmrreader.cpp) retains `ModificationWord` as a uint32 with no selected epoch/timezone. [Scheduler](../src/canon/scanengine.cpp) describes database freshness as unknown and does not use that word to establish current content. [Scheduling report](database-first-scheduling-2026-10-07.md) and corrected [compatibility guide](../docs/parser-compatibility.md) state the same boundary.
findings.limits: Unchanged source statistics and PMR/MDB matching still do not prove database freshness or byte equality. Operation checks are separate.

findings.title: Normalized PMR filename collisions choose the first record
findings.mechanismAndEvidence: [Scheduler](../src/canon/scanengine.cpp) retains candidates, prefers exact spelling, requires a unique compatible identity, and excludes normalized matches spanning distinct physical names. [Scan tests](../tests/tst_canonscan.cpp): `pmr_exact_name_wins_before_normalized_candidates`, `pmr_unique_normalized_name_is_a_fallback`, `ambiguous_pmr_identities_cannot_supply_even_agreeing_metadata`, `normalized_name_does_not_assign_one_record_to_two_files`.
findings.limits: The two case-distinct physical-file test skips on the current case-insensitive temporary filesystem; this is a platform evidence limit, not proof of that filesystem scenario.

findings.title: Database files are not read as a coherent snapshot
findings.mechanismAndEvidence: [Scheduler](../src/canon/scanengine.cpp) compares discovery and later modification times, excludes detected changes, and makes one bounded fallback pass over skipped headers. [PMR](../src/canon/pmrreader.cpp) and [Bento](../src/canon/bentoreader_p.cpp) readers compare device length before/after reading. [Scan tests](../tests/tst_canonscan.cpp): `a_database_changed_after_a_skip_triggers_header_fallback`, `unopened_media_is_rechecked_before_final_selection`.
findings.limits: No native-object/stat/read-handle snapshot check or common PMR/MDB generation qualification is implemented. Same-length writes or replacement preserving mtime can escape these checks. Active-writer NEXIS/NAS coherence remains unestablished.

findings.title: Boolean/timecode merges cannot replace a positive value with false
findings.mechanismAndEvidence: The live path selects typed present observations rather than applying the former positive-only merge. [MXF projection](../src/canon/mxfprojection.cpp) and [OMF projection](../src/canon/omfprojection.cpp) record explicit drop-frame false; [evidence model](../src/mediaevidence.h) resolves eligible present values by priority. [Evidence tests](../tests/tst_mediaevidence.cpp) distinguish false, absent, unreadable and not-read; [MXF projection tests](../tests/tst_canon_mxfprojection.cpp) constrain timecode to associated objects.
findings.limits: No genuine same-identity database-true/header-false specimen is established. Presentation booleans remain projections of the retained evidence; absence is not positive proof of false.

findings.title: Stale editorial values can override a usable same-identity header
findings.mechanismAndEvidence: [Scheduler/selector](../src/canon/scanengine.cpp) preserves source observations and conflicts under the confirmed priorities: Clip Name header→MDB→AVB, Project PMR→MDB→header, Original Bin MDB→header→AVB. Detected changed sources are ineligible. [Scan tests](../tests/tst_canonscan.cpp): `approved_priorities_and_empty_text`, `changed_physical_file_excludes_database_fallbacks`; [connection report](live-connection-2026-10-04.md) records the user-approved policy.
findings.limits: Eligible database editorial values can still win by that policy; their freshness remains unknown. Opening a header does not certify or refresh every editorial field.

findings.title: Every nonempty MXF header is read with the current flag
findings.mechanismAndEvidence: [Scheduler](../src/canon/scanengine.cpp) reads databases first and skips a header only when a usable match supplies required table metadata, including Clip Duration when enabled. Deliberate skips stay `NotRead`. [Scan tests](../tests/tst_canonscan.cpp): `complete_database_does_not_open_media_header`, `incomplete_or_conflicting_table_metadata_reads_header`. [Compatibility](../docs/parser-compatibility.md) and [feature gates](../docs/release-feature-gates.md) now describe this policy; [full corpus report](visible-resolution-2026-10-07.md) records 65 reads and 2,348 unopened headers.
findings.limits: These are measured decisions on the admitted corpus, not equivalent header coverage for every database. Missing, unresolved or unusable database metadata still triggers fallback.

findings.title: The documented64 MiB MXF metadata cap does not exist
findings.mechanismAndEvidence: Removed the fictitious cap and separate-limit-status statement from [compatibility limits](../docs/parser-compatibility.md). The [MXF reader](../src/canon/mxfreader.cpp) validates ranges/types without an application metadata-memory cap; the [retained-memory report](database-first-and-memory-2026-10-07.md) states the agreed policy.
findings.limits: File offset/type validation remains; no new cap or resource-limit outcome has been introduced. Memory acceptance is recorded separately from format correctness.

findings.title: Whole-database and metadata-copy I/O has avoidable cost
findings.mechanismAndEvidence: The live [Bento reader](../src/canon/bentoreader_p.cpp) reads declared ranges from the source device; [MXF reader](../src/canon/mxfreader.cpp) skips essence and compacts retained containers. Database-first [scheduling](../src/canon/scanengine.cpp) avoids most header graphs, and [adapter](../src/canonadapter.cpp) shares the scan receipt. [Memory proof](database-first-and-memory-2026-10-07.md) compares retained graph fingerprints; [final measured report](visible-resolution-2026-10-07.md) records the user's acceptance of 2.40 GB peak and 20,802 ms.
findings.limits: Retaining full database object/value evidence and file-specific dictionary graphs still costs RAM/I/O. Further optimization is deferred by the user; no universal speed or peak-memory improvement is claimed.

findings.title: MXF identity operations accept two byte-order spellings
findings.mechanismAndEvidence: [Canonical conversion](../src/canon/projection.cpp) interprets MXF material fields once at the format boundary; [operation guard](../src/oprunner.cpp) compares exact canonical file identities and established header master associations on the opened handle. [Projection tests](../tests/tst_canon_mxfprojection.cpp): `legacy_aafsdk_ids_follow_the_source_encoding`; [operation tests](../tests/tst_fileoperations.cpp): `real_mxf_identity_is_checked`, `canon_scan_receipt_checks_location_and_header_subset`, `skipped_header_checks_database_file_identity`; [byte-order proof](mxf-identity-byte-order-2026-10-07.md).
findings.limits: Existing journal/request compatibility remains separately defined. Exact Avid identity equality is not byte equality or physical-object continuity; no real alternate-spelling collision specimen was established by the original audit.

findings.title: OMF operations have no format identity recheck
findings.mechanismAndEvidence: [Operation guard](../src/oprunner.cpp) uses the fresh legacy reader/projection over `OpFile::io()` for admitted OMF-era suffixes, including embedded OMF in WAV/AIFF, and compares applicable canonical identities. [Operation tests](../tests/tst_fileoperations.cpp): `real_legacy_header_identity_is_checked`; [operation contract](file-operation-checks.md) distinguishes established header IDs, deliberately skipped headers and unknown optional identities.
findings.limits: Plain WAV/AIFF without an established Avid identity retains filesystem checks. Known applicable identity missing/different on reread stops the item; supported parsing and the agreed scan stamp still do not prove byte equality.

findings.title: Automatic database-rebuild wording is too broad
findings.mechanismAndEvidence: Live [Rebalance confirmation](../src/rebalancedialog.cpp) still promises a rebuild on next project open; [row help](../src/mediafile.h) still says Composer rebuilds at relaunch. [Scope guide](../docs/release-feature-gates.md) distinguishes readable shared/managed trees from MediaCentral coordination.
findings.limits: The live wording does not qualify local/unmanaged versus managed storage. Documentation corrections in this pass do not correct these UI strings; no production edit was made.

findings.title: Format acceptance is broader than native Avid qualification
findings.mechanismAndEvidence: [Managed discovery](../src/canon/discoveryengine.cpp), [layout rules](../src/avidmedialayout.h) and [release scope](../docs/release-feature-gates.md) admit managed families/suffixes without a mandatory OP-Atom certification probe. [MXF reader](../src/canon/mxfreader.cpp) retains partition operational-pattern bytes and read outcomes; [compatibility limits](../docs/parser-compatibility.md) separate readable metadata from essence/container qualification.
findings.limits: No authentication of the authoring app, bitstream/essence certification or complete multi-track profile validation. Misplaced/renamed media is not certified native merely because metadata is readable.

findings.title: Whole-bin MSML membership is not timeline usage
findings.mechanismAndEvidence: The live [AvbParser adapter](../src/avbparser.cpp) uses Canon's whole-bin reference engine. The [reference engine](../src/canon/avbreferences.cpp) also implements explicit selected-sequence scopes and retained reachability issues; [tests](../tests/tst_canonavbreferences.cpp) cover selected roots, unrelated sequences/groups, all referenced group angles, disabled/effect dependencies, cycles and ambiguity. [Feature flags](../src/featureflags.h) keep `kSequenceFilter=false`; [feature guide](../docs/release-feature-gates.md) states that the picker is deferred to v2.
findings.limits: The live UI applies whole-bin references. Sequence engine presence/test coverage does not prove semantic playback usage or that unmatched media is unused; incomplete/unsupported references remain explicit.

findings.title: Hard-coded placeholder identity is assumed never real
findings.mechanismAndEvidence: The live [MDB reader](../src/canon/mdbreader.cpp) retains the value graph; [OMF projection](../src/canon/omfprojection.cpp) admits file mobs through descriptor/object-role relationships and has no former fixed-ID blacklist. [MDB tests](../tests/tst_canonmdb.cpp) preserve repeated/private object/property evidence; [reader report](fresh-mdb-reader-2026-10-04.md) records genuine graph retention.
findings.limits: No dedicated regression using the exact formerly blacklisted UID was located.

findings.title: Supported file suffixes and container subclasses are a subset
findings.mechanismAndEvidence: [Layout/conventions](../src/avidmedialayout.h), [discovery](../src/canon/discoveryengine.cpp) and [release scope](../docs/release-feature-gates.md) explicitly retain `.omf`, `.wav`, `.aif` legacy discovery and omit `.aiff`, `.omfi`, SDII and exchange/timeline expansion. [Bento reader](../src/canon/bentoreader_p.cpp) and [legacy-reader report](fresh-legacy-reader-2026-10-04.md) define admitted container behavior; corrected [compatibility limits](../docs/parser-compatibility.md) distinguish RF64 size-table coverage from remaining legacy limits.
findings.limits: Extended Bento1.1 labels, update overlays and arbitrary custom OMF subclasses remain unsupported/unestablished. Authored RF64 coverage does not establish every historical Avid container variant.

findings.title: Rate display buckets obscure exact nearby rates
findings.mechanismAndEvidence: The live [adapter](../src/canonadapter.cpp) formats the exact retained rational to three decimal places; it does not use the old ±0.01 bucket selector. [DNx lookup](../src/canon/dnxnames_p.h) requires an exact checked operating point; [MXF projection tests](../tests/tst_canon_mxfprojection.cpp): `dnx_alias_needs_the_exact_profile_and_operating_point`, `historical_dnx_operating_points`; [scan tests](../tests/tst_canonscan.cpp) compare equivalent rationals without altering observations.
findings.limits: Three-decimal display is still rounded presentation; exact rational remains evidence and decision input. Explicitly evidenced legacy MDB naming-clock spellings are narrowly mapped.

findings.title: Codec/effect tables and absence-based defaults are empirical
findings.mechanismAndEvidence: [Observation construction](../src/canon/projection.cpp) retains source/object/raw encoding and marks codec/effect inference Derived; editable-name effect inference has an explicit limitation. [MXF](../src/canon/mxfprojection.cpp) and [OMF](../src/canon/omfprojection.cpp) classification gate absence defaults on complete supported owning-object reads. [Scan tests](../tests/tst_canonscan.cpp): `effect_inference_follows_selected_name_without_losing_evidence`; [MXF projection tests](../tests/tst_canon_mxfprojection.cpp): `absent_usage_needs_a_complete_owning_set_not_complete_essence`; [DNx evidence](dnx-codec-evidence.md).
findings.limits: General catalogue mappings do not each carry an independently certified verification level/catalogue revision in every selected observation. Labels do not establish bitstream integrity, plugin availability or future producer support.

findings.title: A unique orphan project is treated as the selected file’s project
findings.mechanismAndEvidence: Live [MXF projection](../src/canon/mxfprojection.cpp) projects tagged projects through linked package attributes and records Preface project metadata. It has no whole-header unique-orphan TaggedValue fallback. Corrected [Project names description](../docs/parser-compatibility.md) removes that old claim. [Projection tests](../tests/tst_canon_mxfprojection.cpp): `ownership_requires_an_explicit_unique_package`, `masters_and_repeated_partitions_remain_separate`.
findings.limits: A dedicated orphan-project-only regression was not located. Preface/ContentStorage active-root qualification remains the distinct open F40; project selection is still subject to the approved source priorities.

findings.title: MXF package discovery is not scoped through the active header root
findings.mechanismAndEvidence: Each MXF partition requires a unique supported Preface to ContentStorage path. Only recorded Packages and EssenceContainerData members can establish ownership; orphan sets stay raw and cannot contaminate candidate uniqueness or metadata. Fresh controls cover absent/damaged/multiple roots, orphan candidates and genuinely rooted captured headers. See [corrections](root-membership-corrections-2026-10-08.md), [bounded genuine roots](root-membership-specimens-2026-10-08.md), [MXF controls](../tests/tst_canon_mxfprojection.cpp) and [final verification receipt](evidence/root-membership-verification-2026-10-08.json).
findings.limits: No universal MXF profile or private-set conformance is claimed. Optional PrimaryPackage or omitted essence-data collections do not invent an owned physical package; unsupported ownership falls back to independently eligible sources.
